content.value_statement: Legacy JavaScript can be verbose, hard to maintain, and difficult to refactor safely. This skill guides ES6+ syntax, async patterns, modules, and functional style.
actual_capabilities: Explains ES6+ syntax including arrow functions, destructuring, spread, rest, template literals, and object literals.
Guides Promise, async/await, retry, timeout, and parallel execution patterns.
Shows functional JavaScript patterns with map, filter, reduce, currying, memoization, composition, and immutable updates.
Covers modern classes, private fields, static members, inheritance, modules, dynamic imports, iterators, and generators.
Summarizes best practices and pitfalls for maintainable JavaScript.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not an automated linter or formatter.
Examples are illustrative and need adaptation for framework-specific projects.
It does not replace security review for production network or data handling code.
It does not include runnable tests or project-specific migration tooling.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Code
use_cases.description: Update older JavaScript syntax while preserving behavior and improving readability.

use_cases.title: Improve Async Flows
use_cases.description: Convert callback or Promise-heavy logic into clear async/await flows with error handling.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Patterns
use_cases.description: Create shared guidance for modules, classes, functional transforms, and immutable updates.

prompt_templates.title: Explain ES6 Syntax
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to replace var, traditional functions, and manual property access with modern JavaScript patterns in my file.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Async Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this callback or Promise chain and suggest an async/await version with clear error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Data Transformations
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build a functional data transformation pipeline using map, filter, reduce, and immutable object updates.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Modernization Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare class, module, dynamic import, iterator, and generator options for this architecture and recommend maintainable patterns.

output_examples.input: Refactor a callback-heavy API client to async/await.
output_examples.output: The response identifies sequential steps, proposes async/await flow, and adds error handling checkpoints without changing observable behavior.

output_examples.input: Improve repeated array loops in a reporting feature.
output_examples.output: The response recommends clear transformation stages, names each data shape, and highlights where immutable updates protect callers.

output_examples.input: Choose module patterns for optional product features.
output_examples.output: The response separates core imports from optional loading, explains tradeoffs, and flags when dynamic imports add unnecessary complexity.

best_practices: Use modern syntax when it improves clarity, not only to reduce line count.
Keep async flows explicit, with clear error handling and predictable concurrency.
Prefer immutable transformations when shared objects or arrays may affect other code.
anti_patterns: Modernizing syntax without preserving existing behavior or tests.
Wrapping simple language features in custom abstractions that hide intent.
Using dynamic imports for ordinary dependencies that load on every path.

faq.question: Does this skill execute JavaScript?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for developers to apply in their own projects.

faq.question: Can it help migrate older code?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to replace older patterns with ES6+ syntax and async/await flows.

faq.question: Does it cover TypeScript?
faq.answer: It focuses on JavaScript. Many syntax and design patterns also apply to TypeScript projects.

faq.question: Can it replace a linter?
faq.answer: No. Use it for guidance, then validate changes with your linter, formatter, and tests.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It notes error handling and mutation risks, but production security still needs review.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
